Food–meal
Food is well established for inﬂuencing oral drug absorption and bioavailability (Welling, 1977; Boullata and Armenti, 2010; Deng
et al., 2017). The potential impact of food on the absorption of a medication is an interaction that all new drug applications to the
US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) are required to describe. The potential interaction can occur for a variety of physicochem-
ical and physiologic reasons. This “meal-effect” occurs because the presence of food changes the conditions within the gut lumen
into which a drug is administered. Following a meal there are changes in gut pH, viscosity, volume, gastric emptying rates, bile ﬂow
and pancreatic secretion that inﬂuence drug dissolution, as well as changes to enterocyte permeability, transport, and metabolism.
The inﬂuences of a meal will be different depending on individual drug properties (e.g., pKa, solubility). There is additionally phys-
iologic variability in drug dissolution and absorption based on the consistency and composition of the meal (Rubbens et al., 2019).
